summary: Alexander Wynne is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Bristol under Paul Williams and Rupert Gethin, and completed his DPhil at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich, later serving as a Junior Research Fellow at St John's College, Oxford (2002–2006).

Alexander Yiannopoulos works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling and with teachers including Karin Myers, Sherab Sangpo, Khenpo Sherab Dorje, Georges B. J. Dreyfus, Tom Tillemans, John J. Makransky, William S. Waldron, Jay L. Garfield, Douglas S. Duckworth, and Sara L. McClintock.

Alexander von Humboldt worked in history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at European University Viadrina, TU Bergakademie Freiberg, the University of Jena, and the University of Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne and Georg Christoph Lichtenberg, and held a post at the University of Jena.

Alexander von Rospatt specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of London and the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, he held posts at the University of Leipzig (attested 1995), the University of Vienna (attested 2001), and the University of California, Berkeley (attested 2011–2026).

Alexander von Staël-Holstein worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Tartu, Berlin, Harvard, and Halle-Wittenberg under Richard Pischel. He held posts at Saint Petersburg State University (1909), Peking University (1918–1929), and the Sino-Indian Institute (c. 1928–1937).

Alexandra David-Néel worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the Royal Conservatory of Brussels and received instruction from Philippe Édouard Foucaux, Swami Bhaskarananda Saraswati, Kazi Dawa Samdup, and Lachen Gomchen Rinpoche.

Alexandra van der Geer specializes in Indology, history, and archaeology. She studied under Karel R. van Kooij, Leendert van Daalen, Henk Bodewitz, Fabio Martini, John de Vos, and Paul Y. Sondaar, and held a visiting post at the International Institute for Asian Studies.

Alexandre Langlois was a scholar in Indology who studied under Antoine-Léonard Chézy. He taught classes at Lycée Charlemagne (c. 1817–1835) and held posts at the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres and Académie de Paris from around 1835 to 1854.

Alexis Sanderson is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied at Oxford and under Swami Lakshman Joo. He was a Domus Senior Scholar at Merton College (1971–1974) and served as Lecturer and Professor at Oxford and All Souls College (c. 1977–2015).

Alf Hiltebeitel specialized in Indology and religious studies. He earned degrees from Haverford College and the University of Chicago, where he studied under J. A. B. van Buitenen and Victor Turner, before spending his career at George Washington University (appointed 1968, 1974, and 1981).
Alf Sommerfelt was a scholar in linguistics. He founded the Norwegian Association for Linguistics in 1924 and served as a professor of linguistics at the University of Oslo from 1931 to 1962.

Alfonsa Ferrari was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Giuseppe Tucci, Carlo Formichi, Theodor Bloch, Louis Renou, Jacques Bacot, and Marcelle Lalou, conducting research and later teaching Sanskrit (1952) at Sapienza University of Rome.

Alfred Bloom worked in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He completed a Ph.D. at Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi, and held posts at the University of Oregon (1961–1970), the Institute of Buddhist Studies (Dean, 1986–1994), and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1970–2017).

Alfred Chilton Pearson was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He completed his schooling at King's College School and Highgate School before studying at Christ's College, Cambridge, under John Peile.

Alfred Cooper Woolner was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Trinity College, Oxford. He served as Principal of Oriental College (1903–1936), Honorary Librarian at Panjab University (c. 1902–1928), and Registrar and Vice Chancellor at the University of the Punjab (1928–1936).

Alfred Cort Haddon studied at King's College London and Christ's College, Cambridge. He held academic posts at the Royal College of Science for Ireland (1880–1901) and the University of Cambridge (1879–1880, 1900–1926).

Alfred Edward Housman was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He attended King Edward's School, Birmingham, and Bromsgrove School, studied at St John's College, Oxford (c. 1877–1881), and held a post at University College London (c. 1892–1911).

Alfred Ernout was a scholar in linguistics. He held academic positions at the University of Lille (1913–1924), the University of Paris (c. 1927–1949), the École Pratique des Hautes Études (c. 1927–1949), and the Collège de France (1941–1951).

Alfred Forke specialized in Sinology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Geneva and Humboldt University of Berlin, later holding posts at the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen (1903–1923), Humboldt University of Berlin (c. 1903–1923), and the University of Hamburg (c. 1923–1935).

Alfred Foucher specialized in Indology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, studying at the École Normale Supérieure and under Sylvain Lévi at the EPHE. He held posts at the EPHE, EFEO, Délégation Archéologique Française en Afghanistan, Commission Archéologique de l'Indochine, and University of Paris.
